QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_3

question.text: Mr. Ramesh has two minor children — Aarav (age 12) and Bhavya (age 8). Aarav earns Rs.45,000 from a singing competition on a TV show, and Bhavya earns Rs.20,000 as interest on a fixed deposit gifted by her grandfather. Which income will be clubbed with Ramesh's income?

answer.text: Both Aarav's and Bhavya's income will be clubbed with Ramesh's income
Only Bhavya's Rs.20,000 will be clubbed (subject to Rs.1,500 exemption); Aarav's income from skill/talent is excluded from clubbing
Neither income is clubbed since both children are below 13 years of age
Only Aarav's income is clubbed since it exceeds Rs.1,500; Bhavya's Rs.20,000 is fully exempt

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 64(1A), minor child income is generally clubbed with the parent having higher total income, but the proviso to the section excludes income earned by the minor from (a) manual work, or (b) any activity involving the application of the minor's skill, talent or specialised knowledge and experience. Aarav's Rs.45,000 from a singing competition arises directly from his talent and is therefore excluded from clubbing in his parent's hands. Bhavya's Rs.20,000 FD interest is passive investment income with no skill component, so it is clubbed with Ramesh — subject to the Rs.1,500 per-child exemption under Section 10(32). The Trap: Option A misses the skill/talent exclusion. Option C invents an age-based blanket exemption (13 years) that does not exist. Option D reverses the logic — it keeps the talent income clubbed and excludes the investment income, the exact opposite of what the law does. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit support that minor income is clubbed under Section 64 with a disability exception, but the specific manual-work / skill-talent exception and the Section 10(32) Rs.1,500 exemption are not on the pages checked. The framing above reflects the standard Income Tax Act treatment as generally applied in industry practice.
